summary.text: A 6-year-and-9-month-old male with a history of cleft lip surgery presented with fever, vomiting, diarrhea and lower abdominal pain persisting for 1 week. CT at another hospital suggested a pelvic abscess associated with appendicitis and he was referred. Blood tests showed an increased inflammatory reaction (leukocytes 19,500/μL, C-reactive protein 23.56 mg/dL) and CT showed appendix wall thickening and a 40 mm × 30 mm low-density area adjacent to the rectum.

Emergent surgery was considered high risk, so pelvic abscess drainage was planned for the second hospital day together with meropenem. EUS showed an abscess adjacent to the rectal wall without visible septa; it was punctured, dilated and a 7-Fr, 4-cm double pigtail catheter was deployed for internal drainage without complications.

CT 12 days after drainage showed almost complete disappearance of the abscess and antibiotics were discontinued the same day. He was discharged on the 14th post-procedure day. On the 19th day part of the stent had prolapsed from the anal verge and it was removed endoscopically. No suggestive recurrence was observed and a laparoscopic appendectomy 3 months after the procedure was followed by a favorable postoperative course.

summary.text: A 5-year-and-6-month-old male with no remarkable history was admitted to another hospital with fever, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain, diagnosed with infectious enteritis and given symptomatic treatment. His symptoms did not improve after 10 days, abdominal CT revealed a suspected pelvic abscess associated with appendicitis, and he was referred.

Blood tests showed an increased inflammatory response (leucocytes 16,600/μL, C-reactive protein 13.1 mg/dL), and ultrasonography and CT showed a 50 mm × 30 mm abscess without septum in the vesicorectal fossa with appendiceal wall thickening. Meropenem was prescribed and symptoms gradually improved, but the abscess did not shrink and CT showed a well-defined cavity with a thick capsule consistent with a mature abscess suitable for drainage.

EUS-guided drainage on the 7th hospital day used a 19G EUS-FNA needle, two guidewires, dilation and two 7 Fr, 4 cm double pigtail catheters without complications. CT on the 14th day confirmed shrinkage and he was discharged. On the 16th post-procedure day partial stent prolapse was found and the stents were removed endoscopically. Laparoscopic appendectomy followed 4 months after the drainage with no evidence of recurrence or complications.
